newsitem.title: USA: Union starts anti-NAFTA radio advertisements.
newsitem.headline: Union starts anti-NAFTA radio advertisements.

text.p: Industrial labour unions will start running a series of radio advertisements this weekend against the North American Free Trade Agreement, painting it as a job loser, the unions said Thursday.

The AFL-CIO's Industrial Union Department, which serves 35 manufacturing unions, is sponsoring the ads, which will run initially in Springfield, Ill. The ads focus on the loss of jobs to Mexican workers under NAFTA, the union group said.
The ads urge listeners to contact members of Congress to voice opposition to new trade legislation that would allow U.S. officials to negotiate an expansion of NAFTA to include Chile.
The labour group said Representative John Shimkus, a Republican from Springfield, sits on the House Commerce Committee, a key panel in dealing with trade matters.

A union spokesman said the anti-NAFTA ads will begin running in Washington next week. The ads will continue through September when the administration plans to submit proposed so-called fast-track trade negotiation legislation.

"We're going to take this message across the country between now and the vote on fast-track," said Peter diCicco, president of the AFL-CIO Industrial Union Department. "Congress should not allow the extension of a trade pact that already is responsible for the loss of nearly 500,000 jobs."

The White House is expected to send to Congress next week a report on the trade agreement, which combines the United States, Mexico and Canada in a trading bloc. The report is expected to put NAFTA in a much more positive light as helping the economies of all three member countries.
